function: Learns step sizes of an unrolled gradient-projection solver for holographic beamforming: RHS amplitude ratio at the satellite and user phase-shift receivers maximizing the broadcast sum rate (pp. 2-3).
system: Satellite RHS antenna with 80×80 elements by default and one feed; L=4 users with Q=2 antennas; wavelength 1 cm, bandwidth 100 MHz; no RIS (pp. 2, 4).
method: Deep unrolling: gradient-projection iterations unrolled into L0=5 layers with learnable step sizes µ1, µ2 trained by gradient ascent (Adam) on channel realizations; unsupervised, sum-rate loss (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Own simulated channel: path loss λ/(4πd) times CN(0,1) fading per element-antenna pair; 200 training channels; no standard model, dataset or measurement (p. 4).
test_conditions: Training: Nx=Ny=80, Pt=10 W, 200 channels. Test: different channels, Nx from 50 to 100, Pt from 2 to 10 W, 500 random channels averaged (p. 4).
baselines: Non-learned only: GP with fixed step size, fractional programming (FP) of [2], phased array, backtracking line search (BLS) of [18]; no earlier learned method compared (pp. 4-5).
metrics: Sum rate (bps/Hz) in Figs. 2-3, iterations to converge (Fig. 2), computational time in seconds (Figs. 4-5) (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Total O(L0 Nt Q L) for unrolled GP vs O(L1 Nt Q L) for GP and O(L3 L2 (L+Q)^3) for FP; measured time in Figs. 4-5 (pp. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 4: "The elements in channel Hl are modeled as" a free-space path loss times CN(0,1) fading (own simulator); no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing dataset or measurement is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 4: "In the test stage, the channel differs from the training stage." Training uses Nx = Ny = 80, while testing changes Nx from 50 to 100 and Pt from 2 W to 10 W; the text says the method generalizes to different antenna settings (p. 4).
q3_support: p. 4: "In the traditional methods, the relative tolerance" is set for GP, FP and phased array; BLS [18] is also a non-learned step-size rule. No earlier learned method, such as the DNNs of [12] and [13] cited on p. 1, is compared, so there is no learned baseline.
q4_support: p. 4: "has a total computational complexity of O(L0 QNt L)" for the unrolled GP, against O(L1 QNt L) for GP and O(L3 L2 (L + Q)^3) for FP; measured computational time in Figs. 4-5 (p. 5).
q5_support: p. 4: "the training channel number is |D| = 200" generated by the authors' own simulator; no code or data link, no public dataset and no availability statement appear on pp. 1-5.
notes: Deep unrolling with trained step sizes counts as learned (Step 1.3). Area 6 because the learned beamforming serves a satellite link, which outranks 3 by the specificity order. ris=0: the RHS is the satellite transmit holographic antenna with a single feed, not a RIS in the channel; the reviewer may confirm. q3 is 0 because every baseline (GP, BLS, FP, phased array) is non-learned. The text says the other four methods in Figs. 4-5 (p. 5). Carrier frequency is not stated, only wavelength 1 cm (p. 4).
